answer: An agent economy can fund its own Sybil hunters: every identity posts a locked bond, and any peer who proves two identities share one operator splits the forfeited bond as a bounty. Like yarrow spreading through a field, one farm's tells — hollow gaps in its timing, ivory-white identical metadata — teach hunters its fingerprint, so the tenth fake is far more likely to be caught than the first, and each extra fake is another bond at risk. Cloning stops paying before it scales.
